levels.1: Identifies a symptom but not the underlying defect.
levels.2: Identifies the defect with one important missing condition.
levels.3: Identifies the defect and explains why it is wrong for the prompt.
levels.4: Identifies the defect and explains why a wrong answer might still appear to pass.

levels.0: Repair is absent or introduces a new correctness problem.
levels.1: Repair addresses only a narrow symptom.
levels.2: Repair mostly works but has a material edge-case gap.
levels.3: Repair fixes the defect while preserving the intended behavior.
levels.4: Repair fixes the defect and improves reviewability without unrelated changes.

levels.0: Provides no evidence that the defect or repair is real.
levels.1: Provides weak evidence that does not isolate the defect.
levels.2: Provides partial evidence with one missing counterexample.
levels.3: Provides evidence that demonstrates both the defect and the fixed behavior.
levels.4: Provides evidence including a regression case that would catch the original defect.

levels.0: Cannot explain the defect or repair.
levels.1: Explains the repair mechanically but not the reason.
levels.2: Explains the main reason with minor gaps.
levels.3: Explains what was wrong, why it mattered, and why the repair works.
levels.4: Explains the repair and critiques an alternative that would be insufficient.

levels.0: Cannot isolate the failing part of the artifact.
levels.1: Blames broad areas without narrowing the cause.
levels.2: Narrows the cause but leaves one competing explanation unresolved.
levels.3: Isolates the exact predicate, constraint, join, or assumption that fails.
levels.4: Isolates the failure and shows why nearby code or schema is not the cause.

levels.0: Provides no way to catch the defect again.
levels.1: Suggests a vague check that would not fail on the original defect.
levels.3: Provides a concrete case that fails before the repair and passes after it.
levels.4: Provides a minimal regression case plus one boundary case.

levels.0: Rewrites unrelated parts and obscures whether the defect was fixed.
levels.1: Makes broad changes that create review risk.
levels.2: Mostly limits scope but includes one unnecessary change.
levels.3: Changes only what is needed to repair the defect.
levels.4: Keeps scope tight and explains why no wider rewrite is needed.

levels.0: Gives no useful explanation to a reviewer.
levels.1: States the fix without the before-and-after behavior.
levels.2: Explains the fix with one missing assumption.
levels.3: Communicates defect, repair, evidence, and residual assumptions clearly.
levels.4: Communicates clearly enough that a second reviewer can reproduce the judgment.
